full_judgment: 6. The plaintiff-opposite party opposed the petition of the defendants under Order VII rule II by filing written objection and on 5-1-75 filed affidavit stating that he applied for re-examination of all his scripts in a typed application and did not scree out the word re-examination and substitute the word "re- scrutinizing" for the word "re-examination" and that there has been some interpolation in his application without his knowledge. The plaintiff opposite party further opposed this application of the defendants under Order 7, rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure by reiterating that the plaintiff's cause of action has been clearly stated in the plaint, that the action of the defendants in the matter of dealing with the plaintiff is motivated and as such without jurisdiction, that the Civil Court has every right to see whether a statutory body has acted in accordance with law, that in the plaint the plaintiff has alleged illegality, arbitrariness and malafide which arc matter of evidence and as such the prayer for rejection of the plaint at such a preliminary stage of a suit is not tenable.
